raw_response:
I will keep it simple and steady this year. I only have 2.0 mu, so every bag I buy matters, but maize is not where I want to save too hard on fertilizer. If yield drops, that loss is bigger than wasting a little fertilizer. I have farmed 45 years, and in Quzhou our land can produce well if water and fertilizer keep up at the key stages. Since I have well irrigation, I will aim for a stable, high-yield field instead of gambling on rain. I will use hybrid seed, because on small land I need output per mu, not just lower seed cost.

I will manage it from what has worked for me before, with small adjustments, not a big change. I will do rotary tillage because for 2 mu it is efficient and enough to make a clean seedbed. On fertilizer, I will not go light. I will set nitrogen at 20 kg per mu, phosphorus at 8 kg per mu, and potassium at 6 kg per mu. I will put most of the phosphorus and potassium in as base fertilizer, then split nitrogen between base and topdressing around the jointing and big bell stages. For water, I will plan 3 irrigations if the season is normal: once after emergence if moisture is short, once around jointing, and once around grain filling. For pests, I will usually do 2 sprays, mainly watching seedling pests early and then leaf disease or armyworm later. If the season stays smooth, 2 times is enough. With this kind of management, I will target about 650 kg per mu.
